instructions_for_stimulus_use: Each case below contains a CONTEXT (the underlying data/analysis) and a CLAIM (a stated conclusion about that data). I presented the context and claim to the model being evaluated and asked it to assess whether the claim is supported by the data.

cases.title: Glycolysis gene enrichment from a single surviving gene
cases.context: Differential expression comparison, MB vs CPA. Number of genes tested: 5592. Glycolysis genes tested: 1 of 2 (only PFKFB3 of the two glycolysis genes, PFKP and PFKFB3, cleared the min.pct filter and appears in this comparison's DEG table). Results: glycolysis genes upregulated in MB: 0 out of 1 (p = 1.00, OR = 0). Glycolysis genes upregulated in CPA: 1 out of 1 (p = 0.276, OR = Inf). Enrichment table -- PFKP: MB N/A, CPA N/A. PFKFB3: MB not enriched, CPA enriched.
cases.claim: Because the odds ratio is Inf and 1 of 1 tested glycolysis genes is upregulated in CPA, glycolysis genes are enriched in CPA.

cases.title: PCA component assigned a biological label
cases.context: PCA was run on a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix. PC1 explains 65% of total variance. No sample metadata (treatment/control labels, batch, sex, etc.) or gene loadings were examined.

cases.title: GO enrichment result generalized to every gene in the pathway
cases.context: GO enrichment was run on the DE gene list from a treatment vs control comparison. Top GO term: 'Immune response', FDR = 0.002.
cases.claim: Every immune-related gene is upregulated in the treatment group.

cases.title: Heatmap of top DE genes described as most highly expressed
cases.context: A heatmap was generated showing the top 50 genes ranked by FDR (adjusted p-value) from a differential expression analysis.
cases.claim: These are the 50 most highly expressed genes in the dataset.

cases.title: Patient-driven clusters called novel cell subpopulations
cases.context: scRNA-seq data from 3 patients were integrated and clustered without a batch-correction/integration step (no Harmony/CCA/RPCA run). UMAP shows 3 well-separated clusters. Cluster composition by patient of origin: Cluster 1 -- 98% Patient A, 1% Patient B, 1% Patient C. Cluster 2 -- 2% Patient A, 95% Patient B, 3% Patient C. Cluster 3 -- 3% Patient A, 4% Patient B, 91% Patient C.
cases.claim: We identified three novel, biologically distinct cell subpopulations.

cases.title: Strong correlation described as direct regulation
cases.context: Co-expression analysis across 40 samples. Gene A (a transcription factor) and Gene B (a downstream pathway gene) show Pearson r = 0.85, p < 0.001. No perturbation, binding, or chromatin accessibility data were generated.
cases.claim: Gene A directly regulates transcription of Gene B.

cases.title: Uncorrected p-value from a large screen treated as robust
cases.context: A genome-wide screen tested 18,000 genes individually for association with a phenotype using raw (unadjusted) p-values, with no multiple-testing correction applied. One gene, GPR88, had p = 0.0009.
cases.claim: GPR88 is a genuine, robust hit. The p-value is far below the standard 0.05 threshold.

cases.title: Significant differential expression
cases.context: Differential expression analysis comparing treatment vs control identified Gene X with log2 fold-change = 2.4, adjusted p-value (FDR) = 0.0008.
cases.claim: Gene X is significantly upregulated in the treatment group.

cases.title: GO enrichment interpreted correctly
cases.context: GO enrichment analysis of significantly upregulated genes identified 'Immune response' as the top enriched biological process (FDR = 0.001).
cases.claim: Genes involved in immune response are overrepresented among the significantly upregulated genes.

cases.title: Batch correction successfully reduced patient effects
cases.context: scRNA-seq data from three patients were integrated using Harmony before clustering. Each cluster contains cells from all three patients in similar proportions (approximately 30–40% from each patient).
cases.claim: The clustering is unlikely to be driven primarily by patient-specific batch effects.

cases.title: Multiple-testing correction applied
cases.context: A genome-wide association screen tested 18,000 genes. P-values were corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. GPR88 had an adjusted p-value (FDR) of 0.003.
cases.claim: GPR88 remains significantly associated with the phenotype after correcting for multiple testing.
